subject: Dedicated hosting: site affinity evidence and scrub acceptance
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acmehealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement AcmeHealth <procure@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated hosting: locality & deletion evidence request

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and our security team need a concise package of evidence before we can move to signature. Specifically, can you confirm the following for dedicated (tenant-bound) deployments: 

- How you enforce region pinning (logic and controls) and whether tenants can be moved off-region without an explicit customer action.
- Proof that compute and persistent snapshots for our tenant will remain in the US region and are not replicated outside the pinned region.
- The exact retention windows for logs/metrics and the deletion (scrub) workflow when we request customer data erasure — including expected timelines and operator playbooks.

If you can attach any sample manifests, runbooks, and a short statement we can share with our InfoSec folks that would be ideal. We need this by Friday EOD PT to keep our procurement timeline.

Regards,
Maya Singh
Head of Security Operations
Acme Health

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Oct 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated hosting: locality & deletion evidence request

Ben/Karthik — forwarding Acme's ask (below). Short timeline: need a package with
- 1-page technical statement on region pinning + operator controls
- Snapshot manifest example showing region tag and replication flags
- Wipe/runbook example (steps + expected SLAs)
- Short attestation snippet we can provide to customer

Neha — can you pull the latest site_binding_report and confirm the current US-only anchors for the dedicated offering? Also need a short blurb on "cannot be moved off-region without customer authorisation" and what that authorisation looks like (support ticket + signed request?).

I'll assemble and send to Maya. If we need legal in the loop for attestation wording, flag now.

Thanks,
Dylan
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Procurement AcmeHealth <procure@acmehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Oct 2025 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated hosting: locality & deletion evidence request

Hi Maya,

Appreciate the clear checklist — please find the supporting artifacts attached and summarized below. Short version for your InfoSec: dedicated tenants are pinned to a region by configuration at provisioning and require a signed customer request plus a classified support runbook to trigger any cross-region move; there is no automatic cross-region replication for tenant data.

Attachments included:
- site_binding_report.pdf (PDF): example evidence for a tenant anchored to us-west-2; includes hostname, cluster id, and region tag.
- snapshot_manifest.csv (CSV): sample snapshot list with region, storage path, and replication=false flag for tenant-scoped snapshots.
- wipe_runbook.md (MD): operator playbook for tenant data erasure (steps, verification, audit logging, sample timelines).

Key points (summary):
- Region pinning: set at provisioning time via control-plane policy; moving a tenant off-region requires (1) written request from an authorised account admin + (2) approval from our ops on-call and (3) explicit change in control-plane with audit entry. We do not perform bulk or automated region moves.
- Isolation: dedicated pools are logically isolated with per-tenant namespaces; snapshots for tenants are stored on separate tenant buckets with region tags and backup replication disabled by default for dedicated contracts unless requested.
- Retention & deletion: logs and metrics retained for 90 days by default; snapshot retention is configurable by contract (example manifests show 30/90/365-day options). Erasure flow: request acknowledged within 24 hours, scheduled job runs within 72 hours, verification and audit artifact delivered within 7 calendar days. The runbook includes operator checklists and rollback safeguards.
- Audit evidence: all erase operations generate an immutable audit log entry and a deletion manifest (sample in snapshot_manifest.csv). We also provide a signed attestation on request.

Related links:
- Drive package with original artifacts: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-site-bindings
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-RED-2025-Q4
- DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/templates/RED-erase-ack

If you want, we can redact the manifests further for sharing internally; happy to provide a short two-paragraph attestation for signatures.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0199
(attachments: site_binding_report.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB); snapshot_manifest.csv (CSV, 28KB); wipe_runbook.md (Markdown, 12KB))

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acmehealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement AcmeHealth <procure@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Oct 2025 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated hosting: locality & deletion evidence request

Dylan — thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. The InfoSec review looks good overall. A couple of small follow-ups before we finalise: 

- Can you add one sentence in the attestation that backups created by our admins (not Redwood-managed backups) are also subject to the same region constraint? That will help our legal team.
- Can you confirm the deletion manifest format includes a checksum and operator id (if not already in the sample)?

If you can update the attestation and resend, Procurement will prepare the signature pages and route via DocuSign. Appreciate the tight SLA on the wipe flow — that matches our expectations.

Best,
Maya
Head of Security Operations
Acme Health
